fieldMarks: Small, fast-flying dabbling duck, about 40–43 cm long
Pale blue wing patch mostly hidden on the water but conspicuous in flight
Spring male has a white crescent on a gray face
In fall many males are in drab eclipse plumage resembling the female
behavior: Migrates late in spring and early in fall; most leave the upper Midwest by early October
Tight flocks twist and turn in unison in flight
Forages in very shallow water, gleaning from the surface; seldom up-ends or feeds away from water
Small groups often stand on stumps or rocks at the water's edge
habitat: Shallow freshwater marshes and ponds in open country, also brackish coastal marshes; in migration and winter any shallow inland or coastal water.
range: Breeds from southern Canada south to California, New Mexico, central Texas, Louisiana and North Carolina, most densely in the prairie pothole region of the north-central U.S. and south-central Canada. Winters from the southern U.S. to South America, more extensively in South America than any other North American dabbler.

lookalikes.name: Cinnamon teal
lookalikes.howToTell: Females of the two species are very similar and hard to separate.
